source_text: Τίνι οὖν, φημί, ἔτι τις χρήσαιτο διδασκάλῳ (??) πόθεν ὠφεληθείη τις. εἰ μηδὲ ἐν τούτοις τὸ ἀληθές ἐστιν; Ἐγένοντό τινες πρὸ πολλοῦ χρόνου πάντων τούτων τῶν νομιζομένων φιλοσόφων παλαιότεροι, μακάριοι καὶ δίκαιοι καὶ θεοφιλεῖς, θείῳ πνεύματι λαλήσαντες καὶ τὰ μέλλοντα θεσπίσαντες, ἃ δὴ νῦν γίνεται· προφήτας δὲ αὐτοὺς καλοῦσιν. Οὗτοι μόνοι τὸ ἀληθὲς καὶ εἶδον καὶ ἐξεῖπον ἀνθρώποις, μήτ᾿ εὐλαβηθέντες μήτε δυσωπηθέντες τινά. μὴ ἡττημένοι δόξης. ἀλλὰ μόνα ταῦτα εἰπόντες ἃ ἤκουσαν καὶ ἃ εἶδον ἁγίῳ πληρωθέντες πνεύματι. Συγγράμματα δὲ αὐτῶν ἔτι καὶ νῦν διαμένει, καὶ ἔστιν ἐντυχόντα τούτοις πλεῖστον ὠφεληθῆναι καὶ περὶ ἀρχῶν καὶ περὶ τέλους καὶ ὧν χρὴ εἰδέναι τὸν φιλόσοφον, πιστεύσαντα ἐκείνοις. Οὐ γὰρ μετὰ ἀποδείξεως πεποίηνται τότε τοὺς λόγους, ἃτε ἀνωτέρω πάσης ἀποδείξεως ὄντες ἀξιόπιστοι μάρτυρες τῆς ἀληθείας· τὰ δὲ ἀποβάντα καὶ ἀποβαίνοντα ἐξαναγκάζει συντίθεσθαι τοῖς λελαλημένοις δι᾿ αὐτῶν. Καίτοι γε καὶ διὰ τὰς δυνάμεις, ἃς ἐπετέλουν, πιστεύεσθαι δίκαιοι ἦσαν, ἐπειδὴ καὶ τὸν ποιητὴν τῶν ὅλων θεὸν καὶ πατέρα ἐδόξαζον καὶ τὸν παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ Χριστὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ κατήγγελλον· ὅπερ οἱ ἀπὸ τοῦ πλάνου καὶ ἀκαθάρτου πνεύματος ἐμπιπλάμενοι ψευδοπροφῆται οὕτε ἐποίησαν οὔτε ποιοῦσιν, ἀλλὰ δυνάμεις τινὰς ἐνεργεῖν εἰς κατάπληξιν τῶν ἀνθρώπων τολμῶσι καὶ τὰ τῆς πλάνης πνεύματα καὶ δαιμόνια δοξολογοῦσιν. Εὔχου δέ σοι πρὸ πάντων φωτὸς ἀνοιχθῆναι πύλας· οὐ γὰρ συνοπτὰ οὐδὲ συννοητὰ πᾶσίν ἐστιν, εἰ μή τῳ θεὸς δῷ συνιέναι καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς αὐτοῦ.
pass_a_gloss: What need, then, is there for a teacher, from whom someone might be benefited, if the truth is not in these things? For there were certain people long before all these supposed philosophers, who were older, blessed, righteous, and loved by God, speaking by the divine Spirit and foretelling what would happen, which is now taking place; and they are called prophets. These alone saw and spoke the truth to people, neither being intimidated nor persuaded by anyone, nor overcome by a desire for glory. But, having been filled with the Holy Spirit, they said only what they heard and saw. Their writings still exist even now, and it is possible for those who encounter them to be greatly benefited, both concerning first principles and the end, and the things that a philosopher should know, by believing them. For they did not establish their words by proof at that time, since they were trustworthy witnesses to the truth, being above all proof. And the things that have happened and are happening compel one to agree with what was spoken through them. And, indeed, they were also worthy of belief because of the powers they performed, since they glorified the Creator of all things, God and Father, and proclaimed the Christ, who is His Son. This is something that false prophets, filled with a deceitful and unclean spirit, have neither done nor do; instead, they dare to perform certain powers to amaze people, and they glorify the spirits of deceit and demons. But I pray that above all, the gates of light may be opened to you, for these things are not understood or perceived by everyone, unless God grants understanding, along with His Christ.

choices.why: The verb ἐπετέλουν is in the imperfect tense, indicating ongoing or repeated action in the past.
The verb συντίθεσθαι means to agree or come to an understanding with someone.
The verb εὔχου is in the present tense, indicating a current or ongoing action.

pass_b_english: What need, then, is there for a teacher from whom anyone could benefit, if the truth is not found in these matters? Long before any of the so‑called philosophers there lived certain men—older, blessed, righteous, and beloved by God—who spoke by the divine Spirit and foretold events that are now occurring; they are called prophets. These alone both saw and declared the truth to humanity, neither intimidated nor swayed by anyone, nor overcome by a desire for glory. Filled with the Holy Spirit, they spoke only what they had heard and seen. Their writings survive to this day, and anyone who reads them can gain great benefit concerning first principles, the end, and all that a philosopher ought to know, provided he believes them. They did not support their words with proof at the time, because they were trustworthy witnesses to the truth, standing above every proof. The events that have happened and continue to happen compel agreement with what was spoken through them. Moreover, they were also worthy of belief because of the powers they performed, since they glorified the Creator of all things, God the Father, and proclaimed the Christ, His Son. False prophets, filled with a deceitful and unclean spirit, have never done this and never do; instead they dare to work certain wonders to astonish people and they glorify the spirits of deceit and demons. I pray that, above all, the gates of light may be opened to you, for these things are not understood or perceived by everyone unless God grants understanding together with His Christ.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, including the distinction between the prophets' actions and those of the false prophets. The translation of 'συντίθεσθαι' as 'agree' is appropriate for the context of being compelled to align with the spoken word. All clauses in the Greek are accounted for in both Pass A and Pass B.

The Greek text is correctly identified as Justin Martyr's 'Dialogue with Trypho 7'. The translation preserves the original meaning, including the distinction between true prophets and false prophets, the role of the Holy Spirit, and the reference to Christ. All key terms are accurately translated, and the scriptural citations are correctly applied. The title 'The Value of Prophets' accurately reflects the content of the passage.
